tasks.title: Build append-only event-log writer with schema and session stamping
tasks.description:
Context: This is change #2 (add-event-log-and-status). improve-cli-ergonomics is assumed already merged (move/edit/assign commands and the list active-marker exist). This lap builds the foundation for the whole event-log capability: a native, best-effort JSONL writer that every mutating command will call in later laps.

Outcome: A reusable event-log writer that appends one JSON line per call to .laps/log.jsonl, populating the full schema and stamping session/scope/file. Not yet wired into any command (wiring is a later lap).

Files & scope: Add a new writer module (a new internal/eventlog package is the natural home; internal/store is acceptable if it fits better — pick one and be consistent). Define the line schema struct and the append helper. Do NOT touch any command file yet. Do NOT add a log reader here.

Design: The writer is NATIVE and BEST-EFFORT by contract: an append failure is reported with a one-line warning on stderr and MUST NEVER change the command's exit code or be returned as an error to the caller. Each line is a JSON object: {ts (UTC RFC3339), event, cmd, file, lap?, title?, assignee?, scope, detail{}, session}. scope defaults to "root". file is the resolved .laps-relative task file (e.g. laps.json, auth.json) for the mutation — the caller passes it in. session is read from the LAPS_SESSION env var and is empty when unset. Optional fields (lap/title/assignee) are omitted or empty when not applicable; detail is an event-specific object (empty object when unused).

Acceptance: Focused unit tests covering: (1) append writes one valid JSON line with all required schema fields populated; (2) session is stamped from LAPS_SESSION when set and empty when unset; (3) scope defaults to root; (4) best-effort on write failure (e.g. unwritable path) — the writer returns no error and emits a stderr note, caller unaffected; (5) appends are additive (existing lines preserved). go test ./... passes.

tasks.title: Fix init gitignore scan to append all missing entries and register log/status commands
tasks.description:
Context: Today internal/cmd/init.go:46-48 breaks out of its scan at the first .laps/claim match, so when .laps/claim is already gitignored the loop never reaches a check for .laps/log.jsonl and the log never gets ignored. Also, the new log and status subcommands must be recognized as built-in commands by the hook dispatcher.

Outcome: laps init scans the COMPLETE .gitignore, appends only the missing entries among {.laps/claim, .laps/log.jsonl}, preserves every existing line, and prints a success message reflecting whichever entries were actually added. log and status are treated as built-in commands.

Files & scope: internal/cmd/init.go (the scan loop around :42-52, the modifiedGitignore decision, and the hardcoded success message at :75), and internal/cmd/hooks.go isKnownCommand switch (add "log" and "status"). Update TestInit / TestInitGitignoreAlreadyExists in internal/cmd/cmd_test.go if their assertions depend on the old single-entry behavior.

Design: Scan the entire file once, collect which of the two target entries are absent, and append exactly those (preserving all original lines and ordering). Replace the hardcoded "Added .laps/claim to .gitignore" message with one that names the entries actually added (e.g. both, just claim, or just log). When neither is missing, keep the existing "Already initialized" path. The isKnownCommand change is a two-token addition to the switch.

Acceptance: A regression test proving the bug is fixed: a .gitignore that already contains .laps/claim still gets .laps/log.jsonl appended by a subsequent laps init. Also: both missing -> both appended; both present -> no change/"Already initialized"; existing arbitrary .gitignore content preserved verbatim. isKnownCommand("log") and isKnownCommand("status") return true. go test ./... passes.

tasks.title: Change claim to structured {lap,file,claimedAt} with back-compat and migrate all callers and tests
tasks.description:
Context: HIGH-RISK core of this change (tasks 5.1, 5.1a, 5.2, 5.3, 5.4, 5.5). The claim file moves off a bare id string to a structured record so status can surface claimedAt. This signature change breaks every reader/writer caller AND existing tests, and the new status command (later lap) depends on this API. A VERIFY lap follows immediately.

Outcome: store.ReadClaim/WriteClaim use a structured store.Claim type; legacy bare-id files read back-compatibly; unknown JSON fields are ignored for forward-compat; malformed structured claims error correctly; every caller and test compiles and passes.

Files & scope: internal/store/claim.go (introduce store.Claim{Lap, File string; ClaimedAt *time.Time}; change ReadClaim/WriteClaim signatures off bare string; implement legacy + malformed logic). Migrate callers: internal/cmd/claim.go (write at :57, read in undo at :79), internal/cmd/done.go (read at :46, re-read before clear at :92), and the list active-marker ReadClaim call added by improve-cli-ergonomics. Migrate tests: internal/store/store_test.go TestClaimCRUD (currently asserts WriteClaim(beadsDir,"test-id-123") and a string round-trip), and the internal/cmd/cmd_test.go done/claim assertions that read store.ReadClaim and compare against "" (around lines 2118, 2143, 2268-2288).

Design: PIN the no-claim sentinel and use it consistently — pick one of {zero-value Claim with Lap=="", (Claim, ok bool), (*Claim nil pointer)} and document it; the existing done.go:51 / claim.go:83 "no claim" branches must keep working. PIN how the legacy bare-id gets its file: ReadClaim must take the caller's resolved selected file as an argument (the store layer does not know it), so a legacy bare-id reads back as {lap: <id>, file: <selected file>, claimedAt: null}; callers pass the selected file. Legacy detection = non-JSON bare token ONLY; bytes that start as JSON (begin with '{') but are malformed or have invalid field types are MALFORMED-claim errors, not legacy. A missing or empty/whitespace claim file remains "no claim" (NOT a malformed error). Ignore unknown JSON fields (e.g. a future scope field) so older readers do not break. WriteClaim should preserve an existing claimedAt when the same lap is reclaimed — expose enough that the claim-wiring lap can implement same-lap reclaim preservation (e.g. read-modify-write, or a preserve flag). Keep done.go:92 re-read-before-clear BEST-EFFORT (a clear failure must not block a completed done).

Acceptance: TestClaimCRUD migrated to the structured API and passing. New store tests: claim records claimedAt; legacy bare-id still read as {lap, file: <selected>, claimedAt: null}; unknown field (e.g. scope) ignored; malformed structured JSON returns a malformed-claim error; missing/empty/whitespace claim file is "no claim" not an error. cmd_test.go done/claim tests migrated and green. go build ./... && go test ./... both clean.

tasks.title: Wire non-claim state-change events into mutating commands
tasks.description:
Context: The event-log writer exists (lap 1) and the structured claim exists (lap 3). Now wire the straightforward state-change events. This is broad but mechanical; the subtler claim-event semantics are a separate SENIOR lap.

Outcome: Each non-claim mutating command appends the correct event(s) after its store save succeeds; read/admin commands emit nothing.

Files & scope: internal/cmd/add.go (created — one event per new lap, including one per lap in a batch --json add), internal/cmd/done.go (completed), internal/cmd/done.go done-undo (reopened), internal/cmd/delete.go (deleted), internal/cmd/prune.go (pruned — one event per pruned lap), and the move/edit/assign commands from improve-cli-ergonomics (moved for move; edited for both edit and assign — there is no assigned event, assign is an edit shortcut, with detail payloads like pos/from/to).

Design: Emit exactly one event per applied state change, and only AFTER store.Save succeeds. Batch commands emit one line per affected lap (batch add -> one created per new lap; prune -> one pruned per removed lap). The writer is best-effort by contract: an append failure warns on stderr and never changes the exit code. Do NOT log read-only or admin commands under any circumstance: get, list, count, status, log, version, help, hook-only commands, init, on, off, update. Stamp cmd, file (resolved .laps-relative file), lap, title, assignee, scope (root), and detail as applicable.

Acceptance: Tests proving: created appended per lap on add (and N created events for a batch of N); completed on done; reopened on done-undo; deleted on delete; one pruned per removed lap; moved/edited with detail on move/edit/assign; reads/admin commands append nothing; a forced log-write failure does not change the command exit code. go test ./... passes.

tasks.title: Wire claim events with reclaim, replacement, and completion-clear semantics
tasks.description:
Context: Claim events have subtle ordering and preservation rules that the structured-claim API (lap 3) now makes possible. Tasks 2.1 (claimed/unclaimed), 2.2, 2.3, 2.4.

Outcome: claim, claim-undo, and done's claim-clear each emit correctly-ordered events with reasons; same-lap reclaim preserves claimedAt and emits no duplicate; a different-lap replacement emits unclaimed(replaced) then claimed; done emits completed then unclaimed(completed); no event is emitted when a claim write/remove fails.

Files & scope: internal/cmd/claim.go (claimed event; same-lap reclaim preservation; different-lap replacement ordering), internal/cmd/claim.go claim-undo (unclaimed event after RemoveClaim succeeds), internal/cmd/done.go (when done clears a claim: emit completed, then immediately unclaimed with detail.reason "completed").

Design: Same-lap reclaim: read the existing claim first; if the target lap is already the claimed lap, preserve the existing claimedAt (do NOT overwrite it) and do NOT emit a second claimed event. Different-lap replacement: emit unclaimed with detail.reason "replaced" for the previously-claimed lap, followed by claimed for the new lap. done clearing a claimed lap: emit completed, then a SEPARATE unclaimed event with detail.reason "completed" (DECIDED: separate event for log uniformity with the replaced reason — one unclaimed per applied claim removal, tagged with the reason). claim-undo: emit unclaimed after RemoveClaim succeeds. For all claim-only mutations, append the event ONLY after WriteClaim/RemoveClaim succeeds; a failed claim write or remove emits no event. All appends remain best-effort.

Acceptance: Tests proving each scenario in the event-log spec: same-lap reclaim preserves claimedAt and emits no duplicate claimed; replacement emits unclaimed(replaced) then claimed in that order; done on a claimed lap emits completed immediately followed by unclaimed(completed); claim-undo emits unclaimed; a failed claim write/remove emits no event. go test ./... passes.

tasks.title: Build laps log reader with filter-then-limit semantics
tasks.description:
Context: Events now flow into .laps/log.jsonl (laps 5-6). Build the reader so operators and Rally can inspect history. Tasks 3.1, 3.2, 3.3, 3.4, 3.5.

Outcome: A laps log command printing recent events human-readable, newest last, with -n, --lap, --session, --since, and --json-output per the DECIDED semantics.

Files & scope: New internal/cmd/log.go (cobra command + reader logic); register it via init(). Add tests to internal/cmd/cmd_test.go. The reader consumes .laps/log.jsonl written by the writer from lap 1.

Design: DECIDED semantics — apply ALL filters first (--lap, --session, --since), THEN truncate to -n (filter-then-limit, so the limit bounds matching events shown, not lines scanned). Default -n is 20. Output is newest-last (chronological order). --since takes an RFC3339 timestamp and is INCLUSIVE of the exact timestamp. Malformed JSONL lines are SKIPPED with a one-line stderr note per offending line and NEVER abort the read (best-effort applied to the reader). --json-output emits a SINGLE object {"events":[...]} (not a bare array). A missing .laps/log.jsonl behaves as an empty log (no error). --lap <id> filters to that lap's full lifecycle. Honor --file to read the log for the selected task file's context as appropriate.

Acceptance: Tests covering task 3.5 — recent events readable; default limit 20 with >20 events; filter-then-limit (--lap <id> -n 5 yields the 5 most recent matching, newest-last); --since RFC3339 inclusive (event whose ts equals the --since value is included); malformed JSONL skipped with a stderr note and reading continues; --json-output emits a single {"events":[...]} object; --lap filters to one lap's lifecycle; missing log is empty not error. go test ./... passes.

tasks.title: Build laps status snapshot with state taxonomy and failure-mode classification
tasks.description:
Context: The structured claim (lap 3) exposes claimedAt, which status now surfaces. This is the second added capability and has subtle failure-mode and JSON-shape decisions. Tasks 4.1, 4.2, 4.3, 4.4, 4.5.

Outcome: A laps status command reporting todo/done counts, the active (claimed) lap, the head lap, the assignee breakdown of todo laps, the selected file identity, and a queue state of active|ready|empty|complete, with correct failure-mode classification and the DECIDED JSON shape.

Files & scope: New internal/cmd/status.go (cobra command + snapshot assembly); register via init(). Consume store.ReadClaim (structured, from lap 3) for claimedAt. Add tests to internal/cmd/cmd_test.go.

Design: State taxonomy — active (a valid todo lap is claimed / work in progress), ready (todo laps exist and nothing valid is claimed), empty (no laps), complete (laps exist, all done). JSON shape DECIDED: expose claimedAt as a nullable RFC3339 UTC timestamp (null when no lap is claimed) and ageSeconds as an integer count of seconds since claimedAt (null when claimedAt is null). DO NOT add a stale boolean in this change (deferred until a threshold/policy is chosen). Failure modes: valid snapshots exit 0; corrupt/unreadable task store, malformed claim JSON, and JSON serialization failures use the NORMAL error path (non-zero), not a hidden healthy snapshot. Dangling claims (claim points at a deleted/pruned/done/wrong-file lap) produce a VALID exit-0 degraded snapshot with claim.valid=false; the system MUST NOT auto-clear such claims silently. Honor --json-output with a stable shape Rally can consume, including the selected file identity.

Acceptance: Tests covering task 4.5 — counts + head reported; empty -> state empty; all done -> complete; todo laps no claim -> ready; claimed valid todo -> active; JSON shape includes file identity and nullable claimedAt/ageSeconds (null when no claim); corrupt store -> error path non-zero; malformed claim -> error path; dangling/non-todo/wrong-file claim -> exit 0 with claim.valid=false and no auto-clear. go test ./... passes.
